text: Saw a LinkedIn Influencer boasting 'Organic Growth' with 75K followers, claiming to help grow your platform, yet copying posts from others. Irony, much?

Jobseekers, this one's for you.

Each application, each interview, each follow-up—it’s exhausting. 
You may wonder: Am I not enough? But remember, it’s not about you or your skills. It’s about a system where 70% of applicants hear nothing back.

Your mental health is more important. 
Take care of yourself, because your dream job is on its way. Until then, pause and breathe. 🌿
Searching for jobs on LinkedIn feels like swiping right on every profile but never getting a match. Ghosted every time!

LinkedIn scams these days: 'Congratulations, you're selected for a job you never applied for!' 
Only condition? Pay Rs. 70,000 upfront. Classic.

Sapne dekhna achi baat hai,
lekin job post dekhke 'interested' likhna,
woh toh sapno ki duniya mein rehna hai, hai na?
Next time I come across a LinkedIn Influencer's long post, I'm reading the last line first. If there's a link, it’s probably fake. Saves time!

Every rejection after 5-6 rounds of interviews felt like a punch in the gut. 
Sleepless nights, hours of preparation, all for nothing—or so I thought.

Looking back, I see those closed doors led to better opportunities.

Each rejection taught me patience, self-worth, and trust. The right door always opens eventually. 
To anyone feeling lost: breathe, trust the process, and know something bigger is coming your way.

To everyone still searching for a job:

I see you. I feel you. 💔

Rejections sting, and the silence after interviews is deafening.

But you're not alone. Over 85% of jobseekers experience self-doubt during this journey. It’s hard, but it’s not the end.

Your worth is not tied to a job offer. Pause, take breaks, and remember: your mental health matters more than any position. 🌱

Let’s break the myth: A big company name doesn’t define talent.

I’ve worked with exceptional people from smaller firms who outperform those at top-tier companies. Your worth isn’t tied to a brand name but your skills and passion.

Freshers, take note: Growth comes from learning, not just a company’s reputation. Focus on mastering your craft and happiness will follow.

When I left a toxic workplace, I told my manager this:

'I hope your son experiences the same leadership you showed me.'

It wasn’t about being petty—it was about showing her what her actions reflected. If she felt bad, it’s because she knew she was wrong.

Let’s aim to be the kind of leaders our kids would be proud to work under.

Break the chain of toxic leadership. Small changes make a big difference. 🙏
